subject: Trouble with Internet Explorer Appearance of NYT Shiny Example

messages.author: 805a107e3320bd82
messages.subject: Trouble with Internet Explorer Appearance of NYT Shiny Example
parts:
Hello
 
I have created the following app (basically a redo of the nyt times Piece)
 
library(shiny)
library(xtable)
library(reshape2)
library(rCharts)
###############################################################################
# Load Systematic Investor Toolbox (SIT)
# http://systematicinvestor.wordpress.com/systematic-investor-toolbox/
###############################################################################
if(!file.exists('../sit'))
  shiny:::download('https://github.com/systematicinvestor/SIT/raw/master/sit.lite.gz', '../sit', mode = 'wb', quiet = TRUE)
con = gzcon(file('../sit', 'rb'))
source(con)
close(con)
library(quantmod)
library(shiny)
runApp("~/CIO_Folder/10_Data_Support_Files/10_R_Code_Files/Shiny/Stock_Charts")
 
where ui and Server are as attached. I get only the attached appearance on my Internet Explorer.
 
In R, it always says "listening on port 8100". R gets stuck there, ie. it is busy, but nothing happens.
 
Can you help me resolving this issue?
 
Best regards
Andreas

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Trouble with Internet Explorer Appearance of NYT Shiny Example
parts:
Sorry but Internet Explorer 9 and earlier is not supported if you simply use Shiny from within R. The Shiny package uses websockets to communicate with the browser, and that technology was not introduced in IE until version 10. 

If you use Shiny Server then IE 8 and 9 are supported (except for fileInput, which is not implemented for those browsers yet). This is because Shiny Server includes technology that emulates websockets using older technologies that are available in those versions of IE.

messages.subject: Re: Trouble with Internet Explorer Appearance of NYT Shiny Example
parts:
Are you sure it's Safari 6 for Windows? From what I'm able to gather from Google, Apple killed Safari for Windows after 5.1.7.

I can confirm that it doesn't work on Safari 5.1.7 on Windows. Safari 5.1 supports an older, draft version of the WebSockets protocol. It's possible that we may add support for the older protocol to httpuv in the future. But in the meantime I recommend trying a recent version of Firefox or Chrome if possible.
